title: Signature Error Beacon
body:
The Signature Error Beacon is Manon's original design for reporting a wrong transfer in the Signature system. The holder lights the beacon on the disputed transfer, which freezes the disputed amount's onward movement, opens an investigation case, and stamps the report with a reference number and a timeline. The beacon stays lit until the investigation closes with written findings, and the holder can watch the case's state at any time, so nobody must chase a person to learn what is happening. The design's rule is that a lit beacon always produces an answer, even if the answer is that the transfer was correct.

Method. The working method for this record is a five-step beacon protocol. First, the holder gathers the transfer's date, amount, account, and expected result. Second, the holder lights the beacon on the transfer, which freezes the disputed amount and opens the case. Third, the case is assigned a reference number and a timeline, visible to the holder. Fourth, the investigation runs and its findings are written into the case. Fifth, if the finding is unfavorable, the holder can request the documents relied on and escalate through the Signature complaint route. The demo prints the beacon steps as a checklist.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature error beacon. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: 1 - gather date, amount, account, expected result; 2 - light the beacon: freeze disputed amount; 3 - receive reference number and timeline; 4 - investigation writes its findings; 5 - if unfavorable, request relied-on documents Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for Signature transfer errors and unauthorized Signature transfers. Do not use it as a claim about any real error-resolution law, because the beacon is a Signature design. Do not use it to delay reporting, because promptness protects the holder's position in any system. title: Signature Bill Lens
body:
The Signature Bill Lens is Manon's original design for reading a Signature statement and finding what does not belong. The lens scans each line against the holder's own records, receipts, and delivery confirmations, and flags lines that match no record, lines whose amounts differ from their receipts, and lines from unknown merchants. Flagged lines are grouped into a dispute bundle with one click, and the bundle carries the evidence for each flag, so the holder disputes with documents, not with a vague complaint. The lens never disputes on its own: it prepares, and the holder decides.

Method. The working method for this record is a four-step lens scan. First, the statement lines are loaded with date, merchant, and amount. Second, each line is matched against receipts and delivery records. Third, unmatched or mismatched lines are flagged with a reason. Fourth, flagged lines are bundled with their evidence for the holder's review. The demo scans a small sample statement and flags the line from an unknown merchant.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature bill lens. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design for Signature statements that need checking before payment. Do not use it as a claim about any real billing-dispute law, because the lens is a Signature design. Do not use it to dispute charges that are merely regretted, because the lens flags errors, not buyer's remorse. title: Signature Record Mirror
body:
The Signature Record Mirror is Manon's original design for checking a Signature credit record against reality. The mirror holds two views side by side: the record as reported, and the holder's own documents, statements, and receipts. Entries that differ, or entries that belong to someone else, shine as mismatches, and each mismatch can be sent as a correction request to both the record keeper and the original furnisher, because correcting with both creates two duties to investigate. The mirror's rule is that the holder's documents are the standard, not the record's confidence.

Method. The working method for this record is a five-step mirror check. First, the holder loads the record and their own documents. Second, entries are compared line by line, and mismatches are marked. Third, for each mismatch, the holder writes what is wrong and what is correct, with documents attached. Fourth, correction requests go to both the record keeper and the furnisher. Fifth, responses are tracked, and uncorrected mismatches can carry the holder's own statement on the file. The demo scans a small sample record and flags the non-current entries.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature record mirror. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: card account -> ok (current); loan account -> CORRECT (unknown account); card account 2 -> CORRECT (late - paid on time per statement) Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design whenever a Signature credit record contains information that is wrong or belongs to someone else. Do not use it to dispute accurate negative information, because the mirror corrects errors, not history. Do not use it as a claim about any real credit reporting law, because the mirror is a Signature design. title: Signature Even Scale
body:
The Signature Even Scale is Manon's original design for fair credit decisions in the Signature system. Every application is weighed on the same scale: creditworthiness factors only, such as payment history and ability to repay, with protected characteristics never placed on the scale. When an application is denied, the scale prints its reasons specifically, so the applicant can check each reason against their own records and ask for reconsideration where a reason is wrong. A scale that cannot print its reasons is not used, because an uncheckable decision cannot be fair.

Method. The working method for this record is a four-step scale check. First, the denial reasons are printed in writing. Second, the applicant compares each reason against their own records. Third, if a reason does not match the record, the applicant asks for reconsideration with the correct information. Fourth, if a pattern suggests the scale itself is tilted, the pattern is documented and escalated through the Signature complaint route. The demo compares two illustrative applicants and flags an outcome difference for review, using clearly labeled illustrative inputs.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature even scale. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: applicant A -> approved; applicant B -> denied; flag for review: True Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design when a Signature credit denial seems wrong or when a pattern of denials seems tilted. Do not use it to claim unfairness from a single denial without evidence, because denials also follow legitimately from credit history and ability to repay. Do not use it as a claim about any real fair-lending law, because the scale is a Signature design. title: Signature Collector Gate
body:
The Signature Collector Gate is Manon's original design for collection contact in the Signature system. No collector reaches a holder without passing the gate, and the gate's rules are strict: the collector must identify itself, state the debt's origin and amount in writing, and stop on a written stop-contact request, with limited exceptions. Harassment, threats, and unreasonable-hour contact are refused at the gate and logged as violations. The holder's side of the gate is a log: every contact, with date, time, caller, and content, kept so that any violation can be shown rather than merely claimed.

Method. The working method for this record is a five-step gate protocol. First, the holder asks for written validation and does not admit or pay on a first call. Second, the holder sends a written validation request and a written dispute if the debt is unfamiliar or wrong. Third, every contact is logged. Fourth, if contact should stop, a written stop-contact request is sent with proof of delivery. Fifth, violations are reported through the Signature complaint route with the log attached. The demo checks a validation checklist and reports what is missing.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature collector gate. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design when contacted by a Signature collector, especially about an unfamiliar debt. Do not use it to ignore a valid debt, because the debt itself does not disappear when contact stops. Do not use it as a claim about any real collection law, because the gate is a Signature design. title: Signature Fee Glass
body:
The Signature Fee Glass is Manon's original design for account fees that cannot hide. Every Signature account's fee schedule is shown through the glass: plain terms, likely fees for the holder's own usage pattern, overdraft rules, and the total cost over a year, all in one view. The glass's rule is that a fee the holder was not shown before choosing the account is a glass failure, and glass failures are correctable through the Signature complaint route. The design treats fee surprises as design failures, not as holder carelessness.

Method. The working method for this record is a fee-glass comparison. First, fee schedules are collected for the accounts being considered. Second, the fees the holder is actually likely to trigger are listed, rather than every fee line. Third, overdraft terms are checked specifically: opt-in rules, per-event cost, and whether fees can stack in one day. Fourth, the likely annual total for the holder's usage pattern is computed. The demo compares two illustrative fee schedules on a stated usage pattern, using clearly labeled design inputs.

title: Signature Servicing Watch
body:
The Signature Servicing Watch is Manon's original design for mortgage-style servicing in the Signature system. The watch tracks every payment, escrow movement, and insurance charge against the agreement, and sounds when a payment is misapplied, an escrow calculation drifts, or paperwork goes missing during a servicer transfer. Servicing errors are the watch's whole subject, because the company collecting payments is not the company that made the loan, and that distance is where errors breed. The holder's protection is the watch's record: written, dated, and checkable against the next statement.

Method. The working method for this record is a five-step watch protocol. First, the holder gathers statements, escrow analyses, and payment proofs, and names the exact error. Second, a written notice of error goes to the servicer's designated address, stating the error and the correction wanted. Third, proof of delivery and copies are kept. Fourth, the servicer's written response is checked against the next statement. Fifth, if the error persists, the case escalates through the Signature complaint route. The demo checks an illustrative escrow calculation and flags a mismatch.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature servicing watch. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: escrow shortfall: 300; flag for servicer review: True Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design when a Signature servicer misapplies a payment, miscalculates escrow, or loses paperwork. Do not use it to stop paying while disputing, because non-payment creates separate consequences even during a dispute. Do not use it as a claim about any real servicing law, because the watch is a Signature design. title: Signature Complaint Ladder
body:
The Signature Complaint Ladder is Manon's original design for escalation in the Signature system. The ladder's rungs are: direct complaint to the firm, with a written narrative and documents; regulator-style review by the Signature oversight desk, which forwards the complaint and requires a company response; and pattern review, where repeated complaints about the same practice are grouped and examined as a practice, not as isolated incidents. Every rung produces a tracked record, so escalation never means starting over, and the ladder's top rung exists precisely for problems that direct complaint could not move.

Method. The working method for this record is a complaint packet. First, a short narrative is written in date order, with amounts and identifiers. Second, key documents are attached: statements, correspondence, and proof of earlier complaints. Third, the remedy wanted is stated plainly. Fourth, the packet is filed through the published channel and the confirmation and case number are kept. Fifth, the company's response is tracked and the complaint updated if the response is incomplete. The demo checks a packet for completeness and lists what is missing.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature complaint ladder. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: packet complete: False; missing: ['prior company complaint proof'] Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design when direct complaints have failed or when a pattern suggests a wider problem. Do not use it as a first step for every issue, because direct, well-documented complaints often resolve faster. Do not use it as a claim about any real regulator, because the ladder is a Signature design. title: Signature Freeze Switch
body:
The Signature Freeze Switch is Manon's original design for locking a Signature credit file. One switch, thrown by the holder, restricts access to the file until the holder lifts it, and the switch must be thrown separately at each Signature record keeper, because a freeze at one keeper does not freeze the others. A companion alert tells potential creditors to verify identity extra carefully before opening an account. The switch does not affect existing accounts or the holder's standing, but it adds a deliberate step whenever new credit is genuinely wanted, which is exactly the friction that stops an impostor.

Method. The working method for this record is a freeze checklist. First, the switch is thrown at each record keeper and the lift credentials are stored securely. Second, an identity theft report is filed where appropriate and kept on file. Third, existing accounts and statements are reviewed for unauthorized activity and disputed where found. Fourth, a fraud alert is set as an additional layer where a freeze is not yet in place. Fifth, switches are lifted temporarily only for specific applications, then restored. The demo checks freeze coverage across three illustrative keepers and reports any gap.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature freeze switch. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: Keeper One -> FROZEN; Keeper Two -> FROZEN; Keeper Three -> NOT FROZEN - throw the switch Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design immediately after discovering identity theft or a serious data exposure in the Signature system. Do not use it as a substitute for disputing fraudulent accounts, because a freeze prevents new accounts but does not remove ones already opened. Do not use it as a claim about any real freeze law, because the switch is a Signature design. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Card Shield
body:
The Signature Card Shield is Manon's original design for unauthorized Signature card use. When a card is lost or transactions appear that the holder did not authorize, the shield is raised: the card locks at once, the unauthorized transactions are listed with date, amount, and merchant, and each is stated plainly as not authorized. The shield's rule is speed: the holder's protection is strongest when the report is fastest, so the shield can be raised from the card itself, without waiting for a phone queue. The investigation then runs against the shield's list, and the holder checks the next statements to confirm the credits are permanent.

Method. The working method for this record is a four-step shield response. First, the card is locked and the loss or unauthorized transactions are reported. Second, every unauthorized transaction is listed with its details and marked not authorized. Third, the holder follows the investigation process, providing any requested statement in writing. Fourth, the next statements are checked to confirm permanent credits and no further unauthorized transactions. The demo lists a sample statement and flags the transactions marked unauthorized.

title: Signature True Cost Table
body:
The Signature True Cost Table is Manon's original design for short-term Signature credit whose single fee looks small but whose total cost is large. The table computes the cost of one term and the cost across rollovers, side by side, so the holder sees the loan's real life instead of its first fee. The table's rule is that cost must be shown as a total and as a rate, in writing, before signing, because a fee without a term is a number without meaning. The holder then compares the total with alternatives, such as a community loan, a payment plan, or assistance, before deciding.

Method. The working method for this record is a total-cost comparison. First, the fee, term, and rollover terms are collected in writing. Second, the cost of one term and the cost across typical rollovers are computed. Third, the total is compared with alternatives. Fourth, the applicable caps or prohibitions in the holder's jurisdiction are checked, since rules vary. The demo computes the cost of an illustrative short-term loan across one term and three rollovers, using clearly labeled design inputs.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature true cost table. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: terms: 1 total fees: 75 total repaid: 575; terms: 3 total fees: 225 total repaid: 725 Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design before taking any high-cost Signature loan, and when helping someone evaluate one. Do not use it to claim any particular loan is unlawful, because legality depends on the product and the rules that apply. Do not use it as financial advice. title: Signature Study Loan Watch
body:
The Signature Study Loan Watch is Manon's original design for study-loan servicing in the Signature system. The watch tracks payments, plan calculations, and forgiveness paperwork against the agreement, and sounds when a payment is misapplied, a plan is miscalculated, or paperwork goes missing. The holder's protection is the watch's file: every statement, every application, and every servicer response, kept in date order, so any dispute starts from documents rather than from memory. The watch routes each issue to its next step: servicer complaint, ombudsman-style review, or regulator-style complaint.

Method. The working method for this record is a five-step watch protocol. First, the exact error is identified and the proving documents gathered. title: Signature Portfolio Lens
body:
The Signature Portfolio Lens is Manon's original design for investment account problems in the Signature system. The lens reconciles statements against trade confirmations and the account agreement, and flags unauthorized trades, unsuitable recommendations, missing statements, incorrect balances, and fees that do not match the agreement. The lens addresses conduct and accuracy, not market outcomes: it cannot say whether an investment was wise, but it can say whether the account did what the holder instructed and what the agreement promised. Flagged items are bundled with their documents for complaint to the firm and, if unresolved, to the Signature oversight route.

Method. The working method for this record is a four-step lens protocol. First, statements, trade confirmations, and the agreement are gathered, and the exact problem is identified. Second, a written complaint goes to the firm stating the problem and the remedy wanted. Third, the firm's response is checked against the documents, because firms sometimes answer a different question from the one asked. Fourth, if unresolved, the case is filed with the oversight route with the full file attached. The demo reconciles a small illustrative statement against confirmations and flags the mismatch.

title: Signature Vehicle Deal Table
body:
The Signature Vehicle Deal Table is Manon's original design for vehicle financing in the Signature system. The table compares loan offers by total cost over the full term, not by monthly payment alone, because a longer term lowers the payment while raising the total. The table also checks the contract for add-ons and for any clause allowing terms to change after signing, and it flags the two classic problems: financing that supposedly falls through after the buyer takes the car home, and add-ons packed without clear consent. The holder keeps a complete signed copy and checks the first statement against it.

Method. The working method for this record is a total-cost comparison plus a contract check. First, offers are compared by total cost over the full term. Second, the contract is read for add-ons and term-change clauses. Third, a complete signed copy is kept and the first statement checked against it. Fourth, if terms changed or add-ons were packed, a written complaint goes to the dealer and lender, and the case can escalate through the complaint ladder. The demo compares two illustrative vehicle loans by total cost, using clearly labeled design inputs.

title: Signature Evidence Vault
body:
The Signature Evidence Vault is Manon's original design for dispute files in the Signature system. The vault holds statements, contracts, correspondence, payment proofs, and a dated log of every contact, with copies stored separately from originals so the file survives a lost device. The vault's rule is that disputes are decided on documents, so the vault answers, without further digging, the questions every dispute process asks: what happened, when, for how much, what was promised, and what has already been tried. A vault built early, while documents are at hand, is far stronger than one reconstructed months later.

Method. The working method for this record is a vault assembly. First, core documents are collected: statements for the disputed period, the agreement, and receipts. Second, correspondence is collected: complaint letters, responses, and proof of delivery. Third, a one-page timeline in date order is written, so any reader can follow the story in minutes. Fourth, copies are stored separately from originals. Fifth, the vault is checked for completeness before filing, and gaps are filled while they still can be. The demo scores a sample vault and lists its gaps.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature evidence vault. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design for any Signature financial dispute, and ideally before a dispute arises, by keeping statements and contracts in one place as a habit. Do not use it to fabricate or alter evidence, because a vault's value is its honesty, and altered documents destroy credibility. title: Signature Scam Tripwire
body:
The Signature Scam Tripwire is Manon's original design for the moments after a Signature scam, focused on stopping further loss, preserving rights, and reporting, in that order. When tripped, the tripwire locks accounts, freezes onward movement of disputed funds where the rail allows, opens a recovery case, and lists the reporting steps with reference numbers to collect. The tripwire is honest about recovery: money already sent over hard-to-reverse rails is often difficult to recover, while card and bank rails sometimes offer dispute routes if reported quickly, so speed is the tripwire's whole point.

Method. The working method for this record is a sequenced tripwire plan. First, further payments stop, contact with the scammer is cut, and accounts are secured with new passwords, stronger authentication, freezes, and fraud alerts. Second, the bank or card issuer is told at once, asking about dispute routes for each payment rail used. Third, reports go to law enforcement and to the consumer reporting channel, with reference numbers kept. Fourth, evidence is preserved: messages, receipts, account numbers used, and the scammer's contact details. Fifth, statements and credit files are watched for follow-on misuse. The demo sequences the steps and prints them in order.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature scam tripwire. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: 1 - stop payments and cut contact; 2 - secure accounts: passwords, freezes, alerts; 3 - report to bank or card issuer at once; 4 - report to law enforcement and the consumer channel; 5 - preserve evidence and watch statements Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design immediately after discovering a Signature scam, even if recovery seems unlikely, because reporting protects others and preserves whatever dispute routes exist. Do not use it to promise recovery, because many scam payments cannot be reversed. Do not use it as a claim about any real recovery service, because the tripwire is a Signature design.
